summary: Valganciclovir is an oral prodrug of ganciclovir, a deoxynucleoside-analogue inhibitor of cytomegalovirus (CMV) DNA polymerase, used to treat and prevent CMV disease (e.g., CMV retinitis in AIDS and CMV prophylaxis in solid-organ transplant recipients). It carries a boxed warning for severe hematologic toxicity (leukopenia, neutropenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia, aplastic anemia), impairment of fertility, fetal toxicity, and potential mutagenicity/carcinogenicity. It must be taken with food, requires renal dose adjustment, and demands frequent monitoring of blood counts and renal function. Pediatric dosing uses a body-surface-area and creatinine-clearance formula.
indications: Treatment of CMV retinitis in adults with AIDS (valganciclovir tablets)
Prevention of CMV disease in high-risk kidney, heart and kidney-pancreas transplant patients (adults)
Prevention of CMV disease in pediatric kidney transplant patients (4 months-16 years) and heart transplant patients (1 month-16 years) at high risk

dosage.d: 900 mg twice daily for 21 days, with food

dosage.n: Within 10 days of transplant; duration per organ/protocol

dosage.d: Once-daily dose (mg) = 7 x BSA x CrCl (modified Schwartz), oral solution 50 mg/mL
dosage.n: Kidney 4 mo-16 y until day 200; heart 1 mo-16 y until day 100
Monitor renal function; not for hemodialysis with standard oral dosing

admin: Take with food to optimize absorption
Do not substitute valganciclovir tablets for ganciclovir capsules on a one-to-one basis
Adjust the dose for renal function and monitor creatinine; oral solution must be constituted by the pharmacist
Handle as a potential teratogen/carcinogen - avoid breaking/crushing tablets and avoid skin/mucous-membrane contact with broken tablets or powder
Avoid if ANC <500 cells/microliter, platelets <25,000/microliter, or hemoglobin <8 g/dL
moa: Valganciclovir is the L-valyl ester prodrug of ganciclovir; after oral absorption it is rapidly hydrolyzed to ganciclovir. In CMV-infected cells, viral and cellular kinases phosphorylate ganciclovir to its triphosphate, which competitively inhibits CMV DNA polymerase and incorporates into viral DNA, halting chain elongation and viral replication.

absolute: Clinically significant hypersensitivity (e.g., anaphylaxis) to valganciclovir or ganciclovir
relative: Pre-existing bone-marrow suppression or concurrent myelosuppressive therapy/irradiation
monitor: Complete blood counts with differential and platelets (frequently)

preg: Valganciclovir is converted to ganciclovir, which is teratogenic, embryotoxic and causes fetal/maternal toxicity in animals at exposures around twice human levels; it has the potential to cause birth defects in humans. Avoid in pregnancy; advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during and for at least 30 days after therapy, and males to use condoms during and for at least 90 days after.
lact: Breastfeeding is not recommended during valganciclovir therapy because of the potential for serious hematologic toxicity and cancer in the nursing infant (and HIV transmission risk in HIV-positive mothers).
renal: Valganciclovir requires dose reduction in renal impairment, adjusted to creatinine clearance; ganciclovir is renally cleared and accumulates, increasing toxicity. Monitor renal function and adjust accordingly; ganciclovir is dialyzable.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dose adjustment is provided.

major: Imipenem-cilastatin - generalized seizures reported with ganciclovir; coadministration not recommended
Other myelosuppressive/nephrotoxic agents (zidovudine, mycophenolate, dapsone, hydroxyurea, pentamidine, amphotericin B, flucytosine, doxorubicin) - additive marrow/renal toxicity; monitor
moderate: Cyclosporine or amphotericin B - monitor renal function
Mycophenolate mofetil - increased risk of hematologic and renal toxicity in renal impairment
minor: Renally excreted drugs - increased levels in renal impairment; monitor
interactions.food: Take with food to enhance bioavailability.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; avoid if it adds to nausea, dizziness or CNS effects.
interactions.diagnostics: Frequently causes neutropenia, anemia and thrombocytopenia, and may raise serum creatinine.

serious: Severe myelosuppression - neutropenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia, pancytopenia, aplastic anemia

monitoring: Complete blood counts with differential and platelet counts frequently (more so in infants, renal impairment, prior cytopenia)
Serum creatinine / renal function and dose adjustment
counsel: Take it with food and exactly as prescribed; do not stop without advice
Frequent blood tests are needed because this drug can lower your blood counts and affect your kidneys
It can cause birth defects and infertility - women should use reliable contraception during and for 30 days after; men should use condoms during and for 90 days after
Do not break, crush or handle broken tablets or the powder with bare skin; wash off any contact
Report fever, sore throat, easy bruising/bleeding, unusual tiredness, seizures or confusion; avoid driving if you feel dizzy or confused; do not breastfeed
pk: Rapidly converted to ganciclovir after absorption; antiviral effect within the dosing interval
Ganciclovir Tmax ~1-3 hours; bioavailability ~60% with food
Ganciclovir elimination half-life ~4 hours (longer with renal impairment)
Once- or twice-daily dosing per indication
Store dry powder at 20-25 C; store constituted solution refrigerated 2-8 C and use within 49 days; do not freeze
pearls: Boxed warning: hematologic toxicity, impaired fertility, fetal toxicity, and mutagenesis/carcinogenesis
Oral prodrug of ganciclovir - take WITH food and do not interchange 1:1 with oral ganciclovir capsules
Must reduce dose for renal impairment and monitor CBC and creatinine frequently
Avoid imipenem-cilastatin (seizure risk) and watch additive toxicity with other myelosuppressive/nephrotoxic drugs
Hold if ANC <500, platelets <25,000, or Hgb <8 g/dL; consider growth factors for severe cytopenia
missed: If a dose is missed, take it with food as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule - do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Overdose may cause increased renal toxicity and severe hematologic toxicity (pancytopenia, marrow failure), hepatotoxicity, gastrointestinal toxicity and neurotoxicity (tremor, seizures). Maintain adequate hydration; because ganciclovir is dialyzable, hemodialysis can reduce serum concentrations. Consider hematopoietic growth factors and provide supportive care.
